correctness.rationale: For T nonidentity with B=1-T singular, x*y=y has probability |ker B|/|A| strictly intermediate. When B is invertible, H0 and H1 permute the finite coefficient term set, forcing translations by T B^k and thereby all of Z[T]. A nonunit in a nonfield coefficient ring gives an intermediate two-variable equation. For a field all nonzero term differences are onto, proving the dichotomy at arbitrary arity. Faithful scalar action yields A=F_(p^d)^s; displacement groups yield conjugacy and centralizers for the orbit counts. Independent small-field term closure/rank tests and small-cardinality orbit checks returned VERIFY_OK. The proof does not infer infinite statements from finite checks.

value.rationale: The quasigroup branch of a recent groupoid equational-spectrum problem contains a canonical algebraic family of affine quandles. The theorem gives a complete all-orders field-coefficient classification with explicit two-variable obstruction for every excluded case, recovers every nonprojection isomorphism class, and computes labeled operation counts. Repeated irreducible blocks furnish nonsimple examples, indicating genuine structure beyond straightforward simplicity tests. It does not claim general quasigroup classification.
